1.explanation: PaletteTexture.js stores a single WebGLTexture in its private field `texture_` and only calls `gl.createTexture()` when `texture_` is null. When the layer is removed, its renderer is disposed (and its context objects invalidated) but the PaletteTexture instance still holds the old texture. On re-add, `getTexture(gl)` returns the stale texture instead of creating a new one, leading to invalid-context bindTexture errors. In WebGLTileLayer.js, the renderer simply reuses the same PaletteTexture objects passed in via `paletteTextures_` and never resets or deletes them, so the palette is never reinitialized on layer reuse.
1.bug_scenario: After switching the WebGLTileLayer to an NDVI style that uses a palette, repeatedly removing and re-adding the layer causes the tiles to render as a solid black layer. In the browser console you see warnings like “bindTexture: object does not belong to this context”. This happens because the palette textures are created only once (when the layer is first added) and never re-created after the layer (and its renderer) is torn down, so on the next add the code attempts to bind WebGLTexture objects that belong to a now-discarded context.
